That alliance gradually grew into shared laws, trade agreements, public institutions, and—after what historians politely call several energetic disagreements —the federal Republic of Leonia. The founding cities were fiercely independent and had no interest in trading three local rulers for one distant monarch. The republic was therefore built to preserve local identity while giving the cities a common defense and national government. Leonian politics has been arguing over where local freedom ends and federal authority begins ever since. Most citizens consider the arguing an essential public service.
docs.title: Republic of Leonia

docs.text: Each city keeps its own customs and civic identity while participating in the government of the republic. Armskirk sits on the northwestern coast of Leonia's eastern peninsula. It is the current capital: a rain-polished city of government halls, markets, theaters, rail traffic, and confident public opinions. Torath is a mountain city of rail yards, arenas, performance halls, strong cheese, and the serene conviction that everyone else is pronouncing it wrong. Corvos is a coastal city of shipyards, lighthouses, aqueducts, and patient negotiators who consider silence a complete counteroffer. Mian Lung is an older eastern realm that remained separate when Leonia was founded. It later entered a mutual-defense treaty with the republic and became a full province roughly one hundred years ago while retaining a Chancellor and many local institutions. The national capital rotates among the three founding cities every twenty years. Mian Lung participates in the republic but is not part of the capital rotation. Armskirk currently has the privilege, responsibility, and municipal headache of hosting it.
docs.title: The Three Free Cities and Mian Lung

docs.text: Leonian politics borrows its titles from the circus. This is not because government is a joke. It is because Leonians believe power should perform in public, face the crowd, and occasionally be pelted with fruit. The Ringleader is the republic's elected head of government. A Ringleader serves one five-year term and cannot immediately stand for another. The Barker Circle is the executive council. Its members administer the republic and explain its decisions to the public—sometimes in that order. The Jugglers oversee taxes, tariffs, budgets, and trade. They insist the name refers to balancing competing needs, not making public money disappear. The Stagehands oversee roads, rail, civic construction, and other public works. When everything functions, nobody sees them. When it does not, everybody suddenly becomes an engineer. The Audience is the citizen body from which the government draws its legitimacy. Citizens vote, petition, attend debates, cheer, heckle, and maintain the sacred democratic right to complain about the results. The Hall of Accord in Armskirk currently houses the national government. Its public chambers resemble an amphitheater more than a throne room: circular stages, packed galleries, speaking horns, banners, and enough acoustics to make a minor procedural objection sound like a declaration of war.
docs.title: Government

The seat carries a binding vote when national decisions alter the province's levies, military deployments, treaty rights, or the Jade-Lion Concord; otherwise the Chancellor advises the government with all the authority of a very old treaty and an extremely heavy binder. Ringleader Abraham has reached his term limit and is stepping down rather than seeking a way around it. In Leonia, voluntarily leaving office is considered either the highest form of civic virtue or proof that someone has finally read all the paperwork.
docs.title: Current Leadership

docs.text: Every five years, Leonia chooses its next Ringleader through the Trials of the Three Cities . The Trials combine ritual competition, public spectacle, political campaigning, and civic judgment. Teams put forward a candidate for Ringleader and compete before the Audience. The exact sequence, scoring, and oldest rites are intentionally secretive. Some challenges test strength or skill; others test judgment, persuasion, teamwork, or the ability to remain dignified while the entire republic watches. Officials reveal rules when tradition requires it, which is a ceremonial way of saying at the last possible moment . The current Trials opened in Armskirk with a spectacular Super Clash Bros competition. The surviving teams now advance toward a public debate. Beyond that, contestants receive the same reassuring guidance given to generations before them: prepare for anything, trust the judges, and sign the waiver.
docs.title: The Trials of the Three Cities

docs.text: Twenty-five years ago, neighboring Mycoterra was still the Confederated Cap States : thirteen slaveholding states ruled from Richmire by vampire aristocrats. Their laws called slavery Royal Bond Service and sold feeding rights alongside labor contracts. This improved neither the slavery nor the vampires, although it produced considerably more paperwork. Enslaved Mycoterrans and abolitionists built their own liberation movement. Harriet Tubers guided families through the Underground Pipeway , Frederick Sporeglass rallied the country through speeches and newspapers, Ulysses S. Grantoad commanded the Army of the Free Caps, and William Tecumseh Shrooman broke Confederate supply lines during the March to the Green Sea. Young Leonian Lincohn Abraham joined the rebellion as a vampire hunter, wielding his silver-edged axe The Railsplitter against officers who treated death as a brief scheduling conflict. Mian Lung 's Jade Lantern Relief Company carried healers and engineers into the war, and its soldiers' water drums famously summoned Deuce Leem , guardian of Xuán Ji, at Eclipse Ford. The fighting passed through Fort Shroomter, Gettyspore, the Thwomp Trenches, and Eclipse Ford before Operation Breaking Dawn brought down Richmire and Blood Regent Toadstool. The new government abolished slavery, established citizenship, protected voting rights, and rebuilt the country as the Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra . Mycoterrans remain quick to remind foreign admirers that they liberated themselves; Lincohn helped with the unusually persistent vampires.
docs.title: The War of Broken Chains

docs.text: The neighboring Sporeign Dominion of Mycoterra spent twenty years rebuilding after overthrowing the slaveholding vampire government that once ruled it. Five years ago, Mycoterra petitioned to become another Leonian province. Ringleader Abraham vetoed admission under the charter's Free Assent Clause after auditors found suspiciously uniform votes, matching council resolutions, and communities that inspectors could not interview privately. Critics call the veto an old soldier's prejudice; supporters call unanimous politics a contradiction wearing a very cheerful hat. This year's Open Ring Accord is the compromise. Mycoterra may sponsor the Redcap Resolutes for one Trials cycle, led by Marshal Marioni—a Mycoterran reformer who earned Leonian citizenship while rebuilding the Corvos floodworks. If Marioni wins, he may become Ringleader, but Mycoterra must still face a separate admission vote. Leonia has therefore addressed a major foreign-policy dispute in its traditional manner: public arguments, elaborate rules, and controlled property damage.
docs.title: Mycoterra and the Open Ring

docs.text: Mian Lung is Fang Ro's homeland, an eastern coastal province whose history predates the republic. Its merchants, craftspeople, immigrants, and soldiers have shaped Leonia for generations. Mian soldiers form the backbone of Leonian armed forces, while trade and migration have made their traditions part of daily life in the Free Cities. Armskirk's Xiaolong District , or “Little Dragon,” is the most visible expression of that relationship. Founded generations ago by people from Mian Lung, it remains a center for lantern festivals, tea houses, martial schools, bathhouses, artisans, imported goods, and food worth missing a train for. Fang Ro served among Mian Lung's warriors before traveling with the party. General Wei Shen and Black Chao also hail from Mian Lung, and their reputations carry considerable weight among soldiers and veterans in Leonia. Mian Lung is presently facing a wave of fires and disappearances blamed on the Jǐn Bào , or “Golden Leopards,” whose leader Master Zhaoyan preaches purity through flame. Fang Ro has returned home to confront the crisis while Black Chao travels with the party. The Golden Leopards' ultimate purpose remains unknown.
docs.title: Mian Lung and the Eastern Connection

docs.text: The original Leonian pact was forged by Armskirk, Torath, and Corvos about two hundred years ago. Mian Lung was not a founding member. After the republic already existed, the independent Jade Kingdom signed a separate mutual-defense treaty with Leonia and remained a sovereign treaty partner for generations. Roughly one hundred years ago, the Jade-Lion Concord made Mian Lung a full province of Leonia. The Concord preserved the office of Chancellor and a place for Mian Lung in national government while formalizing military, tax, and food obligations. The fact that everyone still argues about which side gave up more is considered proof of a balanced treaty. The Lion Line, a recent joint rail venture with Tinkertown and EARS, has strengthened trade and travel between the republic's cities without turning Leonia into “the railroad nation”—a distinction its tourism office makes with surprising frequency. The capital rotates Corvos → Torath → Armskirk , then repeats; each move loses at least one ministry and several good chairs. Famous former Ringleaders include Louie the Fourteenth-Time , who built fourteen fountains and one working sewer; Vicky Regina , who wore black and doubled the national tea budget; and Otto von Biscuit , who unified the tariff code through pastries and threats.

docs.text: Suvaria ¶ Converted from the original Homebrewery source into portable Markdown. View the published Homebrewery document . Welcome traveler from an antique land. Please sit and tell us of what you have seen. The unheard of monsters, who slither and bite. Tell us of the wondrous items and and artifacts you have found, their mysteries yet to be unlocked. Of the vexing vocations and surprising skills you have seen. Homebrew Rules ¶ Character Alignment - Please track your character alignment using the Ethics and Morality chart . During the game your DM may require you to make an Alignment Check for heroic or evil deeds. Potions - Drinking a potion requires only a bonus action. Force feeding someone else is an action. Drinking the same potion multiple times in succession may require a Constitution saving throw. Flanking - Works the same as Pathfinder 2e . A creature is flat-footed (taking a –2 penalty to AC) to creatures that are flanking it. Lingering Injuries - These injuries will depend on the damage that caused the player to crit fail a saving throw or take damage that brings them below 0 Hit Points. Examples: Minor - Things like broken bones may cause a movement or attack disadvantage until healed during a long rest or use Lesser Restoration to remove the condition. Major - If a limb is destroyed beyond repair you may need to use a prosthetic until you find a cleric powerful enough to cast Regenerate. Curses - Some curses will require special material components in addition to the Remove Curse spell. Spell Material Components - Any spell component worth less than 100 gold or below level 4 is kept in a material pouch and never needs to be resupplied. Item Attunement - When you receive a new magic item that requires attunement you can choose to instantly attune the item if you have an attunement slot available. Attuned items that are traded between party members still require a Short Rest to attune the item to the new owner. Wild Shape Languages - In addtion to understanding languages they know, a wild shaped druid can understand and speak to beasts of the same kind it has turned into as if using the Speak with Animals spell. New Character - Generally, if a player character remains dead or missing for an extended length of time they become an NPC. Consult the DM if you wish to die or play another character. Rule Clarifications ¶ Skills with Different Abilities - We are using this variant rule. Please ask your DM if you have proficiency with a skill and would like to use a different ability for: https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/basic-rules/using-ability-scores#VariantSkillswithDifferentAbilities Healing Spirit - We are using the 2020 Errata for Healing Spirit. It can only heal a number of times equal to 1 + your spellcasting ability modifier: https://www.sageadvice.eu/2020/04/01/xanathars-guide-everything-errata/ Polymorph - While polymorphed you can still identify friend or foe but can be influenced by animalistic urges. You only understand the languages listed in the creature’s stat block. Weapon Group Specializations ¶ Due to the rigorous daily practice it requires, you may only have one weapon group specialization at a time. You may retrain this using a week of downtime whenever you are in a friendly city. If you don't know if a weapon can be used with a specialization please ask your DM. Polearm Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is moved up to 10 feet in a direction of your choice. This is forced movement. When you make an athletics check to shove a mounted foe you have advantage on any attempt to shove the rider off of its mount. Sword Specialization: ¶ When you critically strike the target is made off-balance by your attack, becoming flat-footed (-2 AC) to everyone until the start of your next turn. In place of an attack, you may use your sword to attempt to disarm an opponent of equal or smaller size by using an Athletics or Acrobatics check. Bow Specialization: ¶ If the target of the critical hit is adjacent to a surface, it gets stuck to that surface by the missile. The target is immobilized and must spend it's movement action making a DC 10 Athletics check to pull the missile free; it can’t move from its space until it succeeds. Reduce the AC provided by cover by one degree when attacking with a bow. Brawling Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target’s speed is halved(minimum of 5ft) and it cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. You have advantage on Attack rolls against a target you are Grappling. Axe Specialization ¶ When you critically strike, choose one creature adjacent to the initial target and within reach. You deal damage to that creature equal to the result of the weapon damage die you rolled. This amount isn’t doubled, and no other additional dice apply to this damage. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack roll if you already attempted to attack a different target this turn using this weapon. Club Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target is knocked prone. You deal damage equal to your strength modifier when you make an athletics check to shove a target regardless of if you succeed. Dagger Specialization ¶ When you critically strike the affected target takes 1d8 persistent bleed damage. You gain an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to double the weapon’s item bonus to attack rolls. When you are wielding a dagger weapon, increase the base damage die size of that weapon by one step. Spells ¶ Note: Reward spells require no spell slot unless specified. Crowlies Cromatic Sparks ¶ transmutation spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 120 feet Components: V, M, S (bit of glitter) Duration: Up to 3 hours Uses: 1 per short rest This spell is similar to skywrite except it works a lot better at night since it's just fireworks without the noise. You can also write on buildings and clothing. The smaller the writing the longer it lasts. The color of the sparks is affected by the color of the glitter used. Level 5 : Writing on a surface now lasts 24 hours and you can weave intricate shapes into your writing. Wild Shrooms ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt) Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, while in the forest or underground you touch the dirt and call upon the Mycelium spirits to come to your aid! Suddenly a ring of mushrooms up to 20ft in diameter appears in the designated location. Anyone that walks within a foot of the ring is affected by the mushroom's spores. The size and effects of the mushrooms are determined by what kind they are. (best start studying those now...) Level 5 : Assuming you have been casting this, you are now proficient in mushroom knowledge and have a better idea of what kind of mushrooms you are calling forth. Animated Shroom ¶ conjuration spell Casting Time: 1 bonus action Range: 30 feet Components: V, M, S (dirt, mushroom spore) Duration: Up to 1 hour Uses: 1 per long rest As an action, you instantly grow and animate a mushroom that you control. The mushroom takes on the appearance and taste of whatever type of mushroom spore you used to animate it. The mushroom follows your instructions unless you tell it to do something stupid like jump off a cliff (it is intelligent after all). The mushroom is friendly and stays animated for 1 hour then reverts back into a regular mushroom. You can cast Animated Shroom on it again to reanimate and it will retain its memories from before. Stats (minus the sunlight sickness). https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-sprout-mm.html Level 7 : The mushroom gets stronger https://5e.tools/bestiary/myconid-adult-mm.html Eisenheim's Book of Illusions ¶ Note: Advanced spells only usable by illusionist wizards Illusory Creature ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends. The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows. In combat, the illusion can use 1 action per turn. It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. At Higher Levels: The damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd and the maximum size of creature you can create increases by one (to a maximum of Gargantuan). Blanket of Stars ¶ Illusion spell, level 4 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 10 minutes A flowing cloak of utter darkness drapes over you, filled with pinpricks of light like distant stars. It imparts the stillness of the cosmos to you, granting you a +2 status bonus to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak. While outside under a starry night sky, you're also invisible as long as you remain still. When moving under a starry night sky, you have Advantage on stealth checks instead. Gazing too closely into the stars is disorienting. Any creature that ends its turn adjacent to you must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC; this is a mental, visual effect. On Failure the creature rolls with disadvatage against you until the end of its next turn. Item Facade ¶ Illusion spell, level 1 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 10 feet Components: V, S Duration: up to 1 hour You make the target object look and feel as though it were in much better or worse physical condition. When you cast this spell, decide whether you want to make the object look decrepit or perfect. An item made to look decrepit appears broken and shoddy. An intact item made to look better appears as though it's brand new and highly polished or well maintained. A broken item appears to be intact and functional. Destroyed items can't be affected by this spell. A creature that Interacts with the item can attempt to disbelieve the illusion. Shadow Projectile ¶ Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 reaction Range: 120 feet Components: V, S Duration: Instant You create an illusory duplicate of your ally's ranged attack to confuse your opponents. You launch an illusory double of your ally's projectile or spell at the same target, leaving the enemy unsure which attack to avoid. Target must attempt a Wisdom save against your spell DC. On failure, the target takes 3d8 psychic damage and your ally may roll their attack with Advantage. Regardless of the result of its save, it's temporarily immune to shadow projectile spells for 1 hour. Curses and Boons ¶ Curse of Loviatar (Krunk) ¶ The Maiden of Pain has placed a curse on you making every injury you receive more enjoyable. After a long rest roll a d6, the effect lasts until your next long rest: 1. Nothing happens, you feel as if the curse is weakening. 2. You wake up to find you have stabbed yourself in your sleep somehow, 2d6 damage. 3. First time you are dealt damage in a combat encounter by a melee attack you must make a Wisdom Saving Throw(DC 14). On a fail, you spend your next action attempting to convince your attacker to hit you again and gain resistance to all physical damage. 4. You wake up with a back is covered in welts that toughen your skin. Decrease damage taken by 1d4 for the day. The welts make you vulnerable to Poison Damage. 5. You feel like you stepped on a nail but when you look nothing is there. Reduce movement speed by 10ft due to limp for the day. 6. You wake up and discover you have a painfully large hook body piecing on your head that sharpens your senses. Reduce max health by 1d10 and gain +2 to Consitution Saving Throws. Items ¶ Maul of Maelstroms (Caracus) ¶ Maul, uncommon (requires attunement) You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The bonus damage is lightning damage. Once per long rest you can shout a battle cry and slam an enemy dealing an extra 1d10 thunder damage. They must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked back 10ft and prone. docs.text: Character Alignment - Please track your character alignment using the Ethics and Morality chart . During the game your DM may require you to make an Alignment Check for heroic or evil deeds. Potions - Drinking a potion requires only a bonus action. Force feeding someone else is an action. Drinking the same potion multiple times in succession may require a Constitution saving throw. Flanking - Works the same as Pathfinder 2e . A creature is flat-footed (taking a –2 penalty to AC) to creatures that are flanking it. Lingering Injuries - These injuries will depend on the damage that caused the player to crit fail a saving throw or take damage that brings them below 0 Hit Points. Examples: Minor - Things like broken bones may cause a movement or attack disadvantage until healed during a long rest or use Lesser Restoration to remove the condition. Major - If a limb is destroyed beyond repair you may need to use a prosthetic until you find a cleric powerful enough to cast Regenerate. Curses - Some curses will require special material components in addition to the Remove Curse spell. Spell Material Components - Any spell component worth less than 100 gold or below level 4 is kept in a material pouch and never needs to be resupplied. Item Attunement - When you receive a new magic item that requires attunement you can choose to instantly attune the item if you have an attunement slot available. Attuned items that are traded between party members still require a Short Rest to attune the item to the new owner. Wild Shape Languages - In addtion to understanding languages they know, a wild shaped druid can understand and speak to beasts of the same kind it has turned into as if using the Speak with Animals spell. New Character - Generally, if a player character remains dead or missing for an extended length of time they become an NPC. Consult the DM if you wish to die or play another character.

docs.text: Illusion spell, level 2 Casting Time: 1 action Range: 500 feet Components: V, S Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour You create an illusory image of a Large or smaller creature. It generates the appropriate sounds, smells, and feels believable to the touch. If you and the image are ever farther than 500 feet apart, the spell ends. The image can't speak, but you can use your actions to speak through the creature, with the spell disguising your voice as appropriate. You might need to attempt a Deception or Performance check to mimic the creature, as determined by the GM. This is especially likely if you're trying to imitate a specific person and engage with someone that person knows. In combat, the illusion can use 1 action per turn. It uses your spell attack roll for attack rolls and your spell DC for its AC. Its saving throw modifiers are equal to your spell DC – 10. It is substantial enough that it can flank other creatures. If the image is hit by an attack or fails a save, the spell ends. The illusion can cause damage by making the target believe the illusion's attacks are real, but it cannot otherwise directly affect the physical world. If the illusory creature hits with a Strike, the target takes psychic damage equal to 1d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. This is a mental effect. The illusion's Strikes are nonlethal. If the damage doesn't correspond to the image of the monster—for example, if an illusory Large dragon deals only 5 damage—the GM might allow the target to attempt an immediate Perception check to disbelieve the spell. Any relevant resistances and weaknesses apply if the target thinks they do, as judged by the GM. For example, if the illusion wields a warhammer and attacks a creature resistant to bludgeoning damage, the creature would take less mental damage. However, illusory damage does not deactivate regeneration or trigger other effects that require a certain damage type. The GM should track illusory damage dealt by the illusion. Any creature that touches the image or uses the Seek action to examine it can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. When a creature disbelieves the illusion, it recovers from half the damage it had taken from it (if any) and doesn't take any further damage from it. docs.text: The blink dog is an intelligent canine that takes its name from its ability to blink in and out of existence, a talent it uses to aid its attacks and to avoid harm. Blink dogs harbor a long-standing hatred for displacer beasts and attack them on sight. Culture: Blink dogs tend to live in closely knit packs consisting of related individuals. Much like wolves, these packs are generally comprised of a family unit--a mother, a father, and their children. Unlike wolves, it is not uncommon for a pack to also include extended family members (grandparents, aunts, uncles) and the adult children of the pack, which are welcome to stay and expand the pack by bringing home a mate. Language: Blink dogs have their own language, a mixture of barks, yaps, whines, and growls that can transmit complex information. Combat: Blink dogs hunt in packs, teleporting in a seemingly random fashion until they surround their prey, allowing some of them to take advantage of flanking. Maturation Rate: Blink dogs will mature into an adult at about 10 months(at which point ask me for a new sheet). Warranted Suspicion: Blink dogs tend to be highly suspicious of other races, as the wicked and unscrupulous have long sought their fortune by stealing blink dog pups with the intention of "taming" and "training" them and then selling them for outrageous amounts of coin. Given that blink dogs are sapient creatures the equal of any human, dwarf, or elf, this practice is understandably viewed by blink dogs as kidnapping and slavery. Curious Companions: Although most blink dogs keep strictly to their own kind, some eccentric individuals chose to attach themselves to roving "packs" of adventurers, spurred on by curiosity.

docs.text: White Crane Dojo ¶ Mian name: Baihe Wuguan Location: Xiaolong district, Armskirk Known for: Martial arts, public demonstrations, youth lessons, community defense, and educational soreness The White Crane Dojo teaches crane forms, tiger forms, flowing-river forms, and the ancient beginner's discipline of discovering how flexible you are not. Its whitewashed courtyards and rain-dark practice stones are open to respectful visitors for morning demonstrations, supervised lessons, and tea afterward. The headmaster is Master Shrew Fu , a tiny elderly shrew shifter whose patience is shorter than he is and whose walking staff has never once been used for walking. He teaches timing, leverage, and the comforting principle that a larger opponent is merely a lever with poor judgment. Senior instructor Beakatrice Plume , a red-crowned crane shifter, teaches the dojo's graceful White Crane forms. She can correct a student's posture with one tap of her folding fan and a disappointed silence audible from across the courtyard. Conditioning instructor Jean-Clawed Van Ram teaches high kicks, practical defense, and dramatic split stances. His horns require him to enter several classrooms sideways; he considers this an architectural weakness. Visitors may observe quietly, book a beginner lesson, or ache educationally. Advanced training is also available by appointment and by signing a document acknowledging that “advanced” is not a synonym for “comfortable.”
